newsitem.title: USA: Associate U.S. Attorney General Schmidt resigns.
newsitem.headline: Associate U.S. Attorney General Schmidt resigns.

text.p: Associate Attorney General John Schmidt, the Justice Department's third-ranking official, resigned Thursday to spend time with his family in Chicago.
The resignation, announced by Attorney General Janet Reno, will be effective Jan. 20, inauguration day for President Clinton's second term.

Schmidt, a top U.S. trade negotiator in Geneva before joining the Justice Department in 1994, said he would be a visiting scholar at Northwestern University law school. Department sources said Schmidt, who has close ties to Chicago Mayor Richard Daley, has expressed an interest in running for political office, possibly governor of Illinois.

"I have some other ideas but I'm not going to talk about those here," Schmidt said. Asked if he was considering entering politics, he told reporters, "I do not think this is the right place to talk about those kinds of possibilities."

Schmidt replaced Webster Hubbell, a close confidant of President and Hillary Rodham Clinton who resigned in February 1994 and later pleaded guilty to criminal charges for bilking his former private law partners and clients of about $500,000.
Schmidt was in charge of civil rights, antitrust, environmental law and implementing the 1994 crime bill. He played a key role in funding for 48,000 new police officers.
He said it was a privilege to work for Reno, who announced his resignation at her weekly news briefing.
Clinton has yet to say whether Reno will remain in her post during his second term and she referred questions on her future to the White House.
